strengths: The combination of batch-wide patch competition, low-dimensional persistent memory, and associative retrieval is an interesting architectural contribution. The global workspace offers a potentially useful mechanism for sharing information across images.

Table 1 supports classification improvements under the reported training protocol. AiT-Small improves CIFAR-10 from 79.53% to 83.34% and CIFAR-100 from 53.19% to 56.30%, with parameters increasing from 14.9M to 15.8M. The Base configuration also improves both datasets.

Table 2 contains useful component ablations. Removing the bottleneck reduces CIFAR-10 accuracy from 83.34% to 75.40%, while replacing Hopfield retrieval with cross-attention reduces it to 81.03%. Memory initialization experiments, temperature sensitivity analysis, and slot visualizations provide additional diagnostic evidence.
weaknesses: The central complexity claim is not supported by the specified computation. Attention scores between all M memory slots and BN patches must be computed before top-k selection; input projections and retrieval also depend on input dimensions. Moreover, AiT retains ordinary per-image self-attention. Fixed workspace capacity therefore does not establish input-independent computational complexity. Parameter counts alone, without runtime, FLOPs, or peak-memory measurements, cannot substantiate the claimed computational efficiency.

Important parts of the algorithm remain unspecified. Equation 8 gives an energy minimization objective without the retrieval update, iteration count, stopping criterion, or differentiation procedure. The manuscript also does not explain whether persistent memory is frozen, reset, or updated during evaluation. Because patches are pooled across images, these choices can make predictions depend on test-batch composition and previous batches. This is a material reproducibility and inference-protocol concern.

The load component of the balance loss cannot provide a useful gradient as written. In Equation 5, counting positive pre-mask softmax scores gives a constant count; using post-top-k scores instead produces a discrete indicator with zero gradient almost everywhere. No differentiable approximation or gradient estimator is described. Figures 8–9 show changes during training rather than a matched comparison without the loss, so they do not isolate its contribution to specialization.

The novelty argument overstates the distinction between associative retrieval and attention. The usual fixed-point update for the modern Hopfield energy in Equation 7 is softmax attention with tied memory keys and values, making the claim that retrieval fundamentally differs from attention misleading. The potentially novel contribution lies in the architectural integration; the manuscript does not adequately establish a fundamentally different retrieval mechanism.

Evidence for improved relational association is mixed. On relational Sort-of-CLEVR, AiT achieves 67.74%, below Coordination at 73.43% and CNN+RN at 81.07%, although its non-relational accuracy is strong. These results support the classification contribution more convincingly than the broader claims about enhanced relational processing.

Secondary reporting issues include inconsistent learning rates between Section 5.1 and Table 6 (1e-5 versus 1e-4) and missing variability for the main tables despite averaging three runs. The weak-reject recommendation is driven principally by the unresolved retrieval/inference specification, balance-loss formulation, and unsupported efficiency claim, which currently outweigh the worthwhile classification gains.
